newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy HPI makes bourse debut, Marzotto up.
newsitem.headline: Italy HPI makes bourse debut, Marzotto up.

text.p: Newly formed Italian industrial group Holding Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI) opened at 1,090 lire on first day of quotation on the Milan stock market.
This was above the 1,050 lire theoretical valuation given to the share by the stock market council ahead of its quotation.
HPI, which formally completed its spin-off from financial holding Gemina last week, announced at the weekend it was merging with textiles and clothing group Marzotto.
Marzotto shares began 7.43 percent up at 14,450.

Gemina shares were suspended in pre-bourse trade. They were also suspended on Friday pending the announcement of results and the HPI/Marzotto merger. Gemina closed on Thursday up 1.67 percent at 1,007.

The stock market council had evaluated a reference price for Gemina of 570 lire post spin-off and a council spokesman said the stock had been suspended for falling excessively from that reference price.
By 0910 GMT, HPI shares were quoted at 1128 lire while Marzotto remained at 14,500.

HPI and Marzotto said their merger would create one of the largest textiles and clothing companies in the world and assessed its theoretical turnover for 1996 as 8.24 trillion lire. --Milan bureau +392 66129507
